records.name: Community Mondays at William Way
records.summary: Monday evening gatherings for LGBTQIA+ adults at William Way: a game night, an open mic for queer performers, and a monthly craft night. Each one meets on a different Monday of the month.
records.what_you_do: Play board games, trivia, and card games, perform or watch at the open mic, or learn a new craft from a facilitator.

schedule.text: Game Night on the first Monday, Out of the Box Open Mic on the third Monday, and Kraftin' with Kim on the fourth Monday, 6 to 8 pm

locations.label: St. Luke & The Epiphany (Game Night and Kraftin' with Kim)

first_step.how: Come to a session on the listed Monday; no sign-up is described, so call or email the Center to ask about a session
first_step.basis: Open to adults 18 and up at a set time and place with a named contact; the page calls the gatherings welcoming.

records.notes: Open Mic location is not stated on the page. The calendar links on the page decode to April 20, April 27 and May 4, 2026 at 6 pm, which is the status evidence. Cost is not stated.

records.name: Peer Counseling at William Way
records.summary: Free, private one-on-one talks with trained volunteer peer counselors for LGBTQ+ people. Counselors help with topics like coming out, relationships, family, isolation, substance use, HIV, aging, and legal or health questions, and they can point you to other support.
records.what_you_do: Walk in during the evening hours or call for a short, goal-focused talk; counselors do not diagnose or prescribe, and they can also speak to a group or organization on request.

schedule.text: Phone support Monday to Friday, 6 to 9 pm; in-person walk-ins Monday to Thursday, 6 to 9 pm; no appointment needed

locations.label: Walk-in at St. Luke & The Epiphany

first_step.how: Walk in during the evening hours, or call or email to set up a time
first_step.basis: No appointment needed and clear ways to start by phone, email or walk-in; the page does not say newcomers are specifically welcomed.

records.notes: The page is undated, so status is probably_active. Conflicts: the peer page gives 6 to 9 pm for in-person hours, while the Empowerment page says 5 to 9 pm Monday to Thursday. The resource page lists 215-732-8255 for peer counseling, and the wellness page lists a different email; the peer page's own phone and email are used here.

records.name: Tuesday MorningsOut
records.summary: A weekly Tuesday morning social group for older gay, bisexual, and trans men (50 and up), run by William Way's Elder Initiative. Members meet in person at St. Luke & The Epiphany, and on the last Tuesday of each month the group also meets online.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Tuesday session for company and conversation, or join online on the last Tuesday of the month.

schedule.text: Every Tuesday, 10:30 am to noon, in person; online on the last Tuesday of the month

first_step.how: Come to the Tuesday session in person, or email elders@waygay.org or call 215-732-2220 to ask about the online link
first_step.basis: Open to men 50 and up with a set day, time and place, and a named contact to ask questions.

records.notes: The Elder Initiative page is undated, so status is probably_active. The page limits this group to gay, bisexual and trans men, which is narrower than the Elder Initiative as a whole.

records.name: Thrivers
records.summary: A monthly peer discussion group for people living with HIV, including long-term survivors and others with personal experience of HIV or AIDS. It runs as part of the Elder Initiative, and members talk through topics that matter to them and support each other.
records.what_you_do: Join the monthly session with lunch provided, talk through a chosen topic, and share support with the others in the room.

schedule.text: Last Saturday of each month, 12 to 1:30 pm

first_step.how: Email elders@waygay.org or call 215-732-2220 to ask about the next session
first_step.basis: Open to people with lived experience of HIV, with a named contact and fixed session times; the page does not say how new members are welcomed.

records.notes: The group's own page at waygay.org/thrivers returned 404. Two William Way pages agree on the last Saturday schedule but differ on the time (12 to 1:30 pm on the Elder Initiative page, noon on the elder resources page). The elder resources page also gives 215-720-9415, which is not used here because it conflicts with the Center's main line.

records.name: The Doctor Is In
records.summary: A monthly health talk for LGBTQ+ adults over 50, with a doctor and guest speakers covering topics like Medicare, medicines, nutrition, and end-of-life care. It is run through the Elder Initiative, with lunch provided and a Zoom option.
records.what_you_do: Attend the monthly talk in person or on Zoom, eat lunch, and ask questions of the speaker.

schedule.text: Second Wednesday of each month, noon to 1 pm, in person and on Zoom

locations.label: John C Anderson LGBT Friendly Apartments

first_step.how: Come in person, or join by the Zoom link on the Elder Initiative page; email elders@waygay.org with questions
first_step.basis: Open to adults over 50 with a fixed date, time and named contact; the page does not say whether it is closed to new people.

records.notes: The only dated item is the series kickoff on August 14, 2024, so status is unknown even though the page describes a monthly series. Location conflicts: the Elder Initiative page gives John C Anderson, while the elder resources page names a William Way kickoff and says other locations are not stated. The Elder Initiative page is used here.

records.name: Friday Check In
records.summary: A weekly Friday lunchtime video check-in on Zoom for LGBTQ+ older adults in the Philadelphia area, run by William Way's Elder Initiative.
records.what_you_do: Join the Zoom call each Friday at lunchtime to catch up and check in with others.

schedule.text: Every Friday, 12 to 1 pm, on Zoom

first_step.how: Email elders@waygay.org or call 215-732-2220 to get the Zoom link, which is also on the Elder Initiative page
first_step.basis: Open to LGBTQ+ older adults with a fixed weekly time and a named contact for the link.

records.notes: The page is undated, so status is probably_active. The Zoom link is on the source page and is not copied here.

records.name: Danceteria
records.summary: Twice a week, older adults get moving through dance sessions at John C Anderson LGBT Friendly Apartments, offered by the Elder Initiative.
records.what_you_do: Take part in the dance and movement sessions, and ask the Elder Initiative for the class times and the contact for the class leader.

schedule.text: Twice a week; the days and times are not shown on the page

locations.label: John C Anderson LGBT Friendly Apartments

first_step.how: Email elders@waygay.org or call 215-732-2220 to ask for class times and the leader's contact
first_step.basis: Open to older adults with a published way to ask about joining; class times are not shown on the page.

records.notes: The source names the class leader and gives a personal email address; neither is recorded here, and the Elder Initiative contact is used instead. Days, times and cost are not shown.

records.name: Chronic Disease Self-Management Program
records.summary: A six-session course, new for 2026, led by peers to help people with long-term health conditions manage their health day to day. It is offered through the Elder Initiative; contact the team for this year's session dates.
records.what_you_do: Attend six sessions with a peer leader and learn ways to manage a long-term health condition day to day.

schedule.text: Six sessions; 2026 dates and times are available from the Elder Initiative

first_step.how: Email elders@waygay.org to ask for the 2026 session dates
first_step.basis: Open to join by asking the Elder Initiative; the page gives a contact but no enrollment steps.

records.notes: The page says the program is new in 2026 but gives no session dates, months, or cost. Status is probably_active from that 2026 mention.

records.name: WayGay Talk Space
records.summary: A free online support group for gay, bi, queer, and trans men who love men, ages 18 and up. It meets monthly on Zoom, is hosted with Mango Tree Counseling and Consulting, and focuses on love, relationships, intimacy, and connection.
records.what_you_do: Register for the monthly Zoom session, then talk with other men about relationships, intimacy, and connection.

schedule.text: Last Tuesday of each month, 8:30 pm Eastern, on Zoom

first_step.how: Register through the Zoom sign-up link on the WayGay Talk Space page before the session
first_step.basis: Open to men 18 and up through a free registration; the page does not say whether the group is closed to new members.

records.notes: The page gives only the recurring last Tuesday schedule and no dates. The partner is a private counseling practice, named as published.

records.name: Ours Truly
records.summary: A social and support effort for trans and gender-diverse adults 18 and up at William Way, with affinity meetups, creative projects, and workshops that teach new skills. A bi-weekly newsletter lists what is coming up, including online links.
records.what_you_do: Join an affinity meetup, take part in a creative project, or attend a workshop; sign up for the newsletter to see dates and online links.

schedule.text: Events are listed in a bi-weekly newsletter; the page shows no fixed day or time

first_step.how: Sign up for the bi-weekly Ours Truly newsletter on the William Way trans programs page to see upcoming events and virtual links
first_step.basis: Open to adults 18 and up through a public newsletter sign-up; the page does not describe how new people are welcomed.

records.notes: The program's own page at waygay.org/ours-truly returned 404, so the facts come from the trans programs page. That page is undated, so status is probably_active.

notes: Budget: 2 of 3 WebSearch calls used; 28 WebFetch calls of a possible 60. Start pages read: waygay.org home, /calendar, /community-connections, /recovery, /mondays, /peer, /elders, /trans, /wellness, /empowerment, /talkspace, /trc, /resource, /elder-resources, /pransome, /about, plus elderinitiative.waygay.org (301 to www.waygay.org, followed through the main site). The calendar page lists no group meetings. The community connections page lists the same six recovery meetings as the recovery page. The recovery page says these meetings no longer meet at William Way; the venues are accurate as of December 19, 2025. No groups-that-meet-here page exists on the site that I could find. Searched but not recorded: TransWay, a weekly trans social group. One search summary says it met Thursdays on Zoom around 2022, and another says it meets online Thursday evenings; the current format is unclear and no URL was found, so it is not recorded. Connecting Generations appears only in an archived search summary with no date or URL, so it is not recorded. The archived summary's claim that over 70 groups meet at the Center is not on the current About page, so it is not used. Outside programs named on William Way's elder and community resource pages (AmeriCorps Seniors, Foster Grandparents, city volunteer office, VolunteerMatch, Penn's Village, JFCS older adults, senior centers, SOWN, Alzheimer's Association caregiver groups, PCA Caregiver Support, JEVS 55+, the AA directory) do not meet at William Way and are out of this slice, so they are dropped. Pride 55Plus and SAGE Connect were checked and could not be read (see blocked). The Elder Community Coalition and PCA LGBTQ+ Advisory Council take inquiries at elders@waygay.org, but no meeting or join step is shown, so they are not recorded. Glenn Sykes Video Library (on-demand videos) is not a group and is not recorded. Alcoholics Anonymous appears only as a directory pointer with no meeting shown, so it is not recorded. Conflicts across William Way pages are noted on the affected records. Most William Way programs give no cost, so cost is unknown on most records. Status: undated pages are probably_active, and the recovery meetings are active only from the December 2025 date. Records are published as 15 publish and 8 not_a_group.
